title: A small rliable: IQM, performance profiles, and stratified bootstrap intervals
brief: Build the robust aggregates and interval estimates of Agarwal et al. (2021), and see why a few seeds and a point estimate can't tell two algorithms apart.
hints: iqm pools everything first: np.sort(scores.ravel()), then cut = int(0.25 * n), then the mean of x[cut : n - cut].
performance_profile compares every score with every tau at once: (x[None, :] > taus[:, None]).mean(axis=1). The inequality is strict.
For one task, (x[:, None] > y[None, :]) + 0.5 * (x[:, None] == y[None, :]) is the table of pairwise wins. Average it, then average across tasks.
stratified_resample indexes with two arrays: scores[idx, np.arange(n_tasks)[None, :]], where idx has shape (n_runs, n_tasks). Each column then only reads its own task.
percentile_ci with confidence 0.95 asks np.percentile for 2.5 and 97.5, not 0.025 and 0.975.
